```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
covid <- read.csv("covid19postvaxstatewidestats.csv")
missing <- is.na(covid)
byrow_missing <- apply(missing, MARGIN = 1, sum)
covid_clean <- covid[byrow_missing == 0, ]
```

```{r}
x1 <- sum(covid$vaccinated_cases)
x2 <- sum(covid$unvaccinated_cases)

n1 <- sum(covid$population_vaccinated)
n2 <- sum(covid$population_unvaccinated)

p1 <- x1/n1
p2 <- x2/n2

p <- (x1+x2)/(n1+n2)

SE <- (p*(1-p)*(1/n1+1/n2))^0.5

z <- (p1-p2)/SE

z
```

```{r}
x1 <- sum(covid$vaccinated_hosp)
x2 <- sum(covid$unvaccinated_hosp)

n1 <- sum(covid$population_vaccinated)
n2 <- sum(covid$population_unvaccinated)

p1 <- x1/n1
p2 <- x2/n2

p <- (x1+x2)/(n1+n2)

SE <- (p*(1-p)*(1/n1+1/n2))^0.5

z <- (p1-p2)/SE

z
```

```{r}
x1 <- sum(covid$vaccinated_deaths)
x2 <- sum(covid$unvaccinated_deaths)

n1 <- sum(covid$population_vaccinated)
n2 <- sum(covid$population_unvaccinated)

p1 <- x1/n1
p2 <- x2/n2

p <- (x1+x2)/(n1+n2)

SE <- (p*(1-p)*(1/n1+1/n2))^0.5

z <- (p1-p2)/SE

z
```

**Using the standard normal distribution table, I found all three of the p-values to be less than 0.0001, effectively showing that they are also below the significance level of alpha = 0.05. This means that all three of the null hypotheses have been rejected, providing evidence supporting the alternative hypotheses that vaccinated individuals had lower rates of COVID-19 cases, hospitalizations, and deaths.**
